checks.reason: The source explicitly claims invariants make the graph-restriction injection an isomorphism and uses that assertion for the Galois case of Lemma 5.10 and the mixed-union lifting in Theorems 5.11?5.12. With X=Y=P1, alpha(z)=z^2, A=O(2), m=2 and L=O(2), the canonical second-factor action on e=du dv is sign -1. The invariant pairs on the normalization are (s,-s)e, whereas a regular pair on C[u,v]/(u^2-v^2) must agree at u=0; its invariant image is (ub,-ub)e. The pair (1,-1)e is an explicit cokernel element. All smooth/projective/basepoint-free/finite-flat/Galois hypotheses and m>=n+1 hold. On a curve a codimension-two deletion cannot remove the branch points. Global dimensions 3 versus 5 follow from H0(O(2,2))^G and its anti-invariant one-dimensional kernel.
checks.counterevidence: The unrestricted diagonal restriction is surjective in this example by polynomial multiplication H0(O(2)) tensor H0(O(2)) -> H0(O(4)). Neither Lemma 5.10 nor the main theorems is disproved. A changed abstract linearization is not a verified replacement compatible with the asserted canonical action/trace construction.
